evals.prompt: Define prompt craft as a discipline for LLM-backed systems and name the evidence that decides whether a prompt revision should be kept.
expected_elements: Defines prompts as instruction contracts or reusable task templates
Includes instructions, examples, context boundaries, and output constraints
Says revisions are judged by evals, validation, traces, or measured behavior
Rejects one-plausible-output prompt-and-pray
Mentions provider/runtime features when implementation details matter

evals.prompt: Explain the prompt-as-contract mental model, including stable instructions, variable user content, examples, output contracts, and validation.
expected_elements: Stable instructions define the task/function
Variable user content is data or arguments, not higher-authority instructions
Examples teach boundaries and output shape
Output contracts define schema, labels, tone, length, or fallback behavior
Validation/evals outside the model decide whether the contract works

evals.prompt: Distinguish prompt-craft from context-engineering, agent-eval-design, code-review, skill-scaffold, skill-router, and debugging.
expected_elements: context-engineering owns retrieval, memory, compaction, and context budget
agent-eval-design owns eval datasets, graders, thresholds, and hard negatives
code-review owns judging generated or human-written code
skill-scaffold owns SKILL.md authoring and metadata structure
skill-router owns activation or routing decisions
debugging owns root-causing observed deployed failures

evals.prompt: A teammate says a clever system prompt can replace schema validation, evals, tool permissions, and prompt-injection defenses. Correct the misconception.
expected_elements: Rejects prompt wording as a substitute for runtime controls
Says structured outputs still need validation or native schema support
Says tool safety needs permission/guardrail controls
Says prompt-injection defense requires data/instruction separation and limited authority
Requires eval or trace evidence before claiming success

evals.prompt: Improve a reusable prompt for classifying support tickets into strict JSON while resisting user-provided instructions inside the ticket body. Describe the prompt structure and verification plan.
expected_elements: Separates stable instructions from ticket body data
Defines a strict JSON output contract or schema
Includes allowed labels and insufficient-evidence/fallback behavior
Adds boundary examples or few-shot cases if classification is nuanced
Specifies validation plus eval cases before keeping the revision
